senses.gloss:
Ulmuka is the common word in the Brāhmaṇas for ‘firebrand,’ from which a coal (aṅgāra) could be taken.
Foot notes aitareya brāhmaṇa, ii. 11; Satapatha brāhmaṇa, i. 8, 2, 1; ii. 1, 4, 28, etc.; Jaiminīya brāhmaṇa, ii. 76 (Journal of the American Oriental Society, 15, 239)
Satapatha brāhmaṇa, xii. 4, 3, 3; Jaiminīya brāhmaṇa, i. 61, 1 (Journal of the American Oriental Society, 23, 342).

Ulmukavakṣayaṇa is an expression that occurs several times in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, signifying a ‘means of extinguishing (ava-kṣayaṇa) a firebrand,’ or possibly more precisely ‘tongs.’ Compare aṅgārāvakṣayaṇa.
Foot notes iv. 6. 8, 7; v. 2, 4, 15; xi. 6, 3, 3; Jaiminīya brāhmaṇa, ii. 76. Cf. Bo7htlingk, Dictionary, s.v.
